CONFIDENTIAL
SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
S.I, Special Branch
REPORT
File No. 6442
Station, 30
Date September 19 39.
Subject Reported student agitation in the Pootung Middle School -
present situation
Made by. D.I. Pan Lien Pih Forwarded by R.W. Mac Chee D.S 9

With reference to the attached translation of
correspondence which appeared in the September 17th
issue of the Chinese-American Daily News and in
which allusion was made to a case of abduction of
a student from the premises of the Pootung Middle
School, enquiries have failed to secure any informa-
tion that would give credence to the report.

In the course of enquiries, however, it has been
ascertained that on September 10, 1939, about a week
following the reopening of the current term, Zau
Chi-lan (曹奇嵐), a student of the Junior Middle
School Department of the Pootung Middle School, with
temporary premises at No. 13 Rue Doumer, accompanied
by his family, attended the school and requested
permission from the school authorities to discontinue
his studies which permission was immediately granted
by the latter. Since that day, Zau has not
attended classes at the school which might have given
rise to the speculation that he is missing. This
belief of his schoolmates was given added strength
when taking into account the fact that Waung Mei-yung
(汪曼雲), ex-principal of the school, has changed
his allegiance and has joined the following of Wang
Ching-wei. In this connection it is worthy of
mention that on August 20, 1939, Waung Mei-yung,
relinquished his post as principal of the school
when it became public knowledge that he had gone
over to the Wang Ching-wei clique and appointed one

Chinese-American Daily News dated Sept.16): 17.9.39 (AM)

A STUDENT OF THE POOTUNG MIDDLE SCHOOL REPORTED
MISSING

On September 10, your paper published a letter
captioned "Why not burn the books and bury the literati?"
This prophetic heading is about to materialize.
The letter was written by a student in the
fall term of Junior Middle School Second Year and revealed a fact
which has been admitted by the school officials, including
Wu Tse-ping (吳之屏), the uncle of the traitorous Hwang
Mei-yung (汪曼雲). It is not known how Zau's (曹)
communication to the Press became known to the school;
most probably, pro-Wang students had reported it to their
master.
Yesterday the school hired some strangers who
took Zau away from the school. We do not know how he
has been dealt with. The student did not attend class
to-day. Thus the future of a bright youth has been
sacrificed.
The school has admitted that the surrender
of Hwang Mei-yung was only a personal act and had nothing
to do with the school. They also say that Wu Tse-ping
was engaged by the Board of Directors as Principal, but
they had forgotten that the traitor Hwang had made the
following introductory remarks at the re-opening of the
school: "As I have certain business to undertake, I have
now resigned. The Directors of this school, such as Pan
Kung-chan (潘公展), O.K. Yui (俞鴻鈞), Tu Yueh-sung
(杜月笙) etc. are all away from Shanghai, so I have
invited lawyer Wu Tse-ping to act as Principal ...." Wu
Tse-ping is thus conducting a slavish education in the
Pootung Middle School on behalf of rebel Wang.
I hope students and teachers of the school
who are unwilling to co-operate with the rebels will leave
the school.

A student of the Pootung Middle School
who is unwilling to be a slave.
September 12.
